clue.text: Others are at ease

definitions.meaning: the others are the remainder, everyone else
to be at ease is to relax or repose

explanation.definitionFit: The remainder of a group is its leftover members, and to relax is a verb sense of the same word.

clue.text: Slight incline

definitions.meaning: slight here means thin, slender in build
to incline is to tilt or slope to one side

explanation.definitionFit: A thin, spare person is slender, and to tilt one's body sideways is a second verb sense of the same word.

clue.text: Up-country there's a large expanse of water

indicators.note: in a down clue, up tells the solver to read the country's name from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for the Republic of Ireland

explanation.surface: Somewhere inland, a traveller comes across a big lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' reverses EIRE (the Irish name for Ireland) in this down entry. The result is one of North America's Great Lakes.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the five Great Lakes, a huge body of fresh water between the US and Canada.

clue.text: A music man can get nastier

indicators.note: the clue says the word nastier can become something else, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician is capable of turning more unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can get' signals that the letters of NASTIER can be rearranged. Sir John Stainer was a Victorian English composer and organist, best known for The Crucifixion.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Stainer was a nineteenth-century English composer and church organist, so he counts as a musician.

clue.text: The fool! To importune the German command!

parts.note: to dun is to pester someone for payment
der is a German word for 'the'
to head something is to lead or command it

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry at someone foolish enough to pester a German officer for orders.
explanation.walkthrough: A dun pesters a debtor for money. DER is one German word for 'the'. To head a group is to command it.
explanation.definitionFit: A blockhead or dolt is a stupid person, which is the sense of the exclaimed insult.

clue.text: A writer, and badly treated it's understood

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument, so it stands for a writer

indicators.note: badly suggests the word treated is done wrongly, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An author who was poorly handled realises what is going on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' is the anagram signal; 'A writer' is a pen, the writing tool standing for the writer.
explanation.definitionFit: When an idea has got through to someone, its meaning has been grasped, which is the figurative sense here.

clue.text: The underworld boss coppers let out appears put out

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld
P stands for pence, copper coins in British money
to lease property is to let it out for rent

explanation.surface: A gangland chief is irritated when the police release someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Dis (Pluto) rules the Roman underworld, not a gang. P is pence, the British coppers (small coins), not police.
explanation.definitionFit: To annoy or offend someone leaves them irritated, which is what being put out means.

clue.text: Heads back to deliver a knockout blow

indicators.note: back tells the solver to read the word for heads in the opposite direction

parts.note: nuts is slang for heads

explanation.surface: Boxers' heads are thrown back by a knockout punch.
explanation.walkthrough: NUTS, slang for heads, is read 'back'.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock someone senseless with a blow is to daze them, which is what a knockout does.

clue.text: Drinks supplied for nurses-tea possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could be arranged another way, so they are shuffled

explanation.surface: Nurses' tea break might have been laced with wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges the letters of NURSES-TEA. The answer is a sweet white dessert wine from Bordeaux.
explanation.definitionFit: These are sweet white dessert wines from the Bordeaux region of France, so they are drinks.

clue.text: Places of work. Orders are sent in

indicators.note: to order things is to put them in sequence, so the letters that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: Workplaces receive orders that come in by post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orders' looks like a noun for instructions, but as a verb it rearranges ARE SENT IN.
explanation.definitionFit: These are works where animal hides are cured into leather, so they are industrial workplaces.

clue.text: Born in June, early June

indicators.note: in shows the answer sits inside the run of clue words that follows

explanation.surface: A birth notice records arriving in early June.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'juNE Early'. It is the French word used before a woman's maiden name.
explanation.definitionFit: Placed before a married woman's maiden name, this French word means 'born with the surname'.

clue.text: A little round object given free

indicators.note: a little of the following words means only part of them, so the answer is a run inside them

explanation.surface: A small ball is handed out at no charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A little' takes a run of letters from 'roUND Object'. 'Free' is a verb here, as in freeing a knot.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfasten or loosen a knot or button is to release it, a verb sense of free.

clue.text: Parking-it can cause depression

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for parking on road signs

explanation.surface: Struggling to find a parking space can make a driver miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' looks like low spirits, but here it means a hollow in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A hole or hollow in the ground is a physical dip, a sense of depression.

clue.text: Rate a spring flower

parts.note: speed is a rate of motion
a well is a source of water, like a spring

explanation.surface: An instruction to judge a flower that blooms in spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' is a water source, not the season.
explanation.definitionFit: Veronica is a small blue-flowered plant, often found in lawns and hedgerows.

clue.text: Competent directors will be anything but baffling

parts.note: sound means reliable or competent
a company's directors make up its board

explanation.surface: A capable management team will speak clearly rather than confuse.
explanation.walkthrough: A baffle damps sound; a soundboard amplifies it, so the definition plays on 'baffling' in its acoustic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A resonating panel in a piano or violin amplifies vibration, the opposite of a baffle that deadens noise.

clue.text: Admitting there's confusing order before racing

indicators.note: confusing jumbles the letters of the order named before it

parts.note: the MBE, Member of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

explanation.surface: A punter confesses to mixing up orders ahead of a race meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confusing' jumbles the abbreviation of a British honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire. 'Admitting' means letting in or including.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking something in, as when a theory covers or includes a group of facts, is to accept or include it.

clue.text: Harangues a bride it's awful

indicators.note: awful suggests things have gone badly wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone rants that a bride looks terrible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' rearranges the letters of A BRIDE IT'S.
explanation.definitionFit: These are long bitter verbal attacks or rants, which is what harangues are.

clue.text: Get sound equipment. There's point to that

parts.note: the ear is the body's equipment for hearing sound
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Buying audio gear has a purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound equipment' is the organ of hearing, not hi-fi; 'point' is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: To receive money in return for work is to obtain or gain it, a sense of get.

clue.text: Buns are maybe provided for a honey-eater

indicators.note: maybe says the letters could be arranged differently, so they are shuffled

explanation.surface: Sweet buns are laid on for something that loves honey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges BUNS ARE. The answer is a small Asian bear known for its love of honey.
explanation.definitionFit: The Malayan bear is a small tropical bear famous for raiding bees' nests, so it eats honey.

clue.text: Many a junior is idle

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many
someone junior is under another in rank

explanation.surface: Lots of junior staff are lazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many' gives M, the Roman numeral for a thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: To wander about aimlessly or talk in a rambling way is to drift lazily.

clue.text: Give a talking-to, being direct

definitions.meaning: to speak formally to an audience or a person
to direct a letter is to write the destination on it

explanation.definitionFit: A speech made to a gathering is one sense, and writing the destination on an envelope is the second.

clue.text: English and retiring

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'English and retiring (4)': E + rev(AND) gives the letters, but no word defines the girl's name; the definition seems cut off and a search did not recover it.

clue.text: Put on fresh clothing and made up

definitions.meaning: having changed into new clothes again
made up for a wrong, set it right

explanation.definitionFit: Dressing again is the literal sense, and compensating for an injustice is the second sense of the same word.

clue.text: Accordingly a quarter gave an out-moded call for help

parts.note: so means therefore or accordingly
S, south, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: A ship's distress signal is described as old-fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a quarter' is a compass direction, south. The Morse distress signal has been officially replaced, hence 'out-moded'.
explanation.definitionFit: This Morse code distress signal was superseded by satellite systems in 1999, so it is now outdated.

clue.text: A letter one's written after church

indicators.note: written after places the letter for one following the abbreviation for church

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone writes a letter after attending church.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the Greek letter, the 22nd of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the twenty-second character of the Greek alphabet, so it is a letter.

clue.text: Seeing nothing in big rough area not producing crops

indicators.note: in places the zero letter inside the rearranged word
rough means roughly made, so the word big is jumbled

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A farmer sees no harvest from a large patch of rough ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' rearranges BIG into GBI, and 'in' puts O (nothing) inside it. The answer is the great desert of Mongolia and China.
explanation.definitionFit: This Asian desert is arid land where nothing grows, so it is barren of crops.

clue.text: A lawyer, having the right, is engaged in trade

indicators.note: engaged in means held within, so these letters go inside the word for trade

parts.note: to barter is to trade goods
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A lawyer with legal entitlement works in commerce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaged in' is the container signal: the right and 'is' are held inside the word for trade. In England this lawyer argues cases in court.
explanation.definitionFit: In England this is an advocate who argues cases in the higher courts, a kind of legal professional.

clue.text: A Russian's one form of transport

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A Russian owns a single vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a typical Russian first name, the equivalent of John.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common Russian man's name, so it stands for any Russian.

clue.text: Not drinking-sheltering in the shade

indicators.note: sheltering means covering, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol

explanation.surface: A non-drinker hides from the sun in the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: TT, short for teetotal, means abstaining from alcohol. 'sheltering' is the container signal. 'shade' is a colour here, not shadow.
explanation.definitionFit: A tint is a hue or variety of a colour, which is one sense of shade.

clue.text: Finish after mid-afternoon break

indicators.note: after places the word for finish behind the middle letter
mid takes the centre letter of the word afternoon

parts.note: end means finish

explanation.surface: A tea break is over after mid-afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of AFTERNOON is R; 'after' puts END behind it. 'break' means tear, not a rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To rip something apart is to tear it, a forceful sense of break.

clue.text: A self-satisfied person's quiet outfit

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
a rig is a set of clothes, an outfit

explanation.surface: A smug person dresses in understated clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the musical term piano, meaning soft.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a smugly self-righteous person who is priggish about correct behaviour.

clue.text: Broke down -isn't using a bear, ing

indicators.note: broke down means fell apart, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A machine broke down because it isn't using a ball bearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broke down' rearranges ISN'T USING A. 'bearing' means supporting a load.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding up a weight or carrying a load is supporting it, a sense of bearing.
